ga_palisades_the.blurb: The Palisades is a secluded stretch of the Chattahoochee River corridor in the Atlanta area, downstream of the I-285 and I-75 crossings. Trails run through forested floodplain, ridges and ravines, and large boulders line the river's edge beneath rugged granite cliffs. Nearly everything is bouldering, with a small number of trad, sport and top-rope lines mixed in. Problems run mostly V0 to V4, with a few harder ones up to V10. Bamboo Forest Area holds the most climbs, followed by Mangler Area, with Riverside Cliffs Area and Soviet Cave Area close behind.

md_thurmont_watershed_area.blurb: The Thurmont Watershed is a wooded tract just outside the town of Thurmont, almost surrounded by Cunningham Falls State Park. Top-roping is the main style here, since protection is limited, with a smaller number of trad routes and a set of boulder problems. Most routes sit between 5.6 and 5.11, with a few easier. Cliffs are typically up to about 40 feet tall, and the rock is described as solid and clean. TWS Rocks holds by far the most climbs. Down Range Rocks, which faces north and is shaded, adds walls and big boulders, and Bear Rocks is a more remote outcrop in the far southwest corner, also facing north.

or_main_area_boulders.blurb: Main Area Boulders are the core of the bouldering at Cline Falls, a small basalt crag on the Deschutes River a few miles west of Redmond. Everything here is a boulder problem, from V0 up to a few at V9 and V10, with the greatest number in the V0 to V3 range. Bluff Zone holds the most climbs, with Blobby Zone, River Spot and Projector Sector close behind. At Projector Sector the boulders stay in shade until late afternoon, and the sector mixes very easy slabs with hard projects.

tx_medicine_wall.blurb: Medicine Wall is a limestone bluff in San Antonio, close to the Salado Creek Greenway. The cliffs run up to about 30 meters, and the rock ranges from excellent blue stone to blocky, loose sections. They form one semicontinuous band, and each distinct section is called a wall. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, mostly 5.8 to 5.11, with a good number of boulder problems and only a few trad lines. The cliffs face north, which gives some shade in summer. Metro Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Buda Belly Wall, with New Testament Wall and Old Testament Wall next.
